title: Tokyo
source: DEMO: stops are the day assignments from data/my-settings.json, in plan order, with made-up times. Replace with the itinerary export.

stops.name: Kaminarimon
stops.note: The iconic Thunder Gate marking the entrance to Senso-ji and Nakamise-dori.

stops.name: Nakamise-dori
stops.note: Historic shopping street running from Kaminarimon toward Senso-ji, lined with traditional snacks, souvenirs and small shops.

stops.name: Hoppy Street
stops.note: Open-front izakaya row

stops.name: Senso-ji
stops.note: Tokyo's oldest temple + Nakamise street

stops.name: Asakusa free deck
stops.note: 8F terrace at the Culture Center

stops.name: Taikokan Drum Museum
stops.note: Small specialist museum created by Miyamoto Unosuke Shoten with hundreds of Japanese and international drums, including instruments visitors can actually play.

stops.name: Onigiri Asakusa Yadoroku
stops.note: Tokyo's oldest onigiri shop, est. 1954, small counter behind Senso-ji

stops.name: Wanariya indigo dyeing
stops.note: Casual aizome studio at 1-8-10 Senzoku where you indigo-dye a tenugui (about ¥2,500) or a T-shirt (about ¥3,600) with stencils and wax in roughly 45 minutes; walk-ins taken.

stops.name: Map Camera
stops.note: 6 floors of graded used cameras

stops.name: Yodobashi Camera
stops.note: Mega electronics + film stock

stops.name: Camera no Kitamura - Shinjuku
stops.note: Multi-floor camera shop with junk section and dedicated Leica floor

stops.name: Sekaido
stops.note: 5-floor discount art-supply store

stops.name: Shinjuku Gyoen
stops.note: Former imperial garden with Japanese, English and French sections and a greenhouse; ¥500, closed Mondays, last entry 16:00 in October.

stops.name: HIBIKUS Asakusa Basement
stops.note: Taiko school and workshop studio beneath the headquarters of historic Japanese drum maker Miyamoto Unosuke Shoten.

stops.name: Taiko no Tatsujin arcade
stops.note: Arcade game with a real drum

stops.name: Wurly's by Miyaji Music
stops.note: Newer modular/electronic shop

stops.name: Kanda Myojin
stops.note: Ornate shrine near Akihabara

stops.name: Yushima Seido
stops.note: Confucian temple of black-lacquered halls in a cedar grove beside Ochanomizu station, with the largest Confucius statue in the world; free, about 9:30–16:00 in October.

stops.name: Ochanomizu music street
stops.note: Blocks of instrument shops

stops.name: Shinohara Maruyoshi Furin
stops.note: One of the last two Edo furin makers, in the Satake shopping arcade near Shin-Okachimachi, with two workshops: blow your own glass bell and paint it, or paint a pre-blown one.

stops.name: Jimbocho
stops.note: Kanda-Jimbocho, the world's largest concentration of secondhand bookshops: more than 130 of them along Yasukuni-dori and the lanes off it, most with their stock spilling onto outdoor racks, plus the old-school curry and coffee houses that grew up to feed the students and editors.

stops.name: Ameyoko Market
stops.note: Open-air market food strip

stops.name: Ohya Shobo
stops.note: Antiquarian dealer on Yasukuni-dori since 1882, selling original Edo-period woodblock books, ukiyo-e prints and old hand-coloured maps; 10:00-18:00, closed Sundays and public holidays.

stops.name: Komiyama Shoten
stops.note: Four floors of art dealing on the Jimbocho main street: photobooks on the second floor, fashion magazines, art and design books, posters and prints above and below.

stops.name: Kumihimo Experience by DOMYO
stops.note: Traditional silk-cord braiding workshop using authentic kumihimo equipment at a braiding house founded in 1652.

stops.name: Koishikawa Korakuen
stops.note: Tokyo's oldest surviving Edo garden (1629), Chinese-influenced, with a full-moon bridge and a miniature Arashiyama; ¥300, 9:00–17:00.

stops.name: Game Center Mikado
stops.note: Floors of vintage arcade cabinets

stops.name: Fujiya Camera
stops.note: 80-year dealer at Nakano Broadway

stops.name: Capyneko Cafe Kichijoji
stops.note: The original Capyneko location, combining free-roaming cats with a capybara in the same space.

stops.name: Gotoku-ji
stops.note: Soto Zen temple said to be the origin of the maneki-neko, with thousands of white beckoning cats stacked beside the pagoda; grounds free, about 6:00–18:00.

stops.name: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building
stops.note: Free observation decks at 202m in Tange's iconic twin towers, with panoramic views of Tokyo and Mt. Fuji on clear days.

stops.name: Omoide Yokocho
stops.note: Smoky lantern alley of tiny counters

stops.name: Nakano Broadway
stops.note: Four floors of roughly 300 tiny specialist shops stacked above a 1966 apartment block, named after Manhattan's Broadway and sold at the time as the most advanced building in Asia, with singers and actors living in the flats upstairs. Most shops run 12:00-20:00 and a few close Wednesdays.

stops.name: Jackroad
stops.note: Pre-owned and vintage watch dealer on the 3F of Nakano Broadway, trading since 1987 and holding over 6,000 watches at any time; 11:00-20:30, with sister shop Bettyroad alongside it.

stops.name: Mandarake Nakano Broadway
stops.note: Mandarake's home ground: more than a dozen shops scattered through the building, each given over to one thing - vintage manga, animation cels, sofubi figures, retro toys, idol photos, secondhand game cartridges.

stops.name: GoodWatch78
stops.note: Antique Rolex specialist on the 3F of Nakano Broadway dealing in vintage references, loose parts and consignment sales; short hours, roughly 13:00-18:00. Their site is goodwatch78.com, served over plain http.

stops.name: Quark Nakano Broadway
stops.note: Branch of the Rolex specialist chain Quark on the 3F of Nakano Broadway; the chain keeps a published antique and vintage Rolex stock list online.

stops.name: Kamekichi
stops.note: Long-running multi-brand dealer at Nakano Broadway with a large Rolex and antique section and multilingual staff; also carries Tudor, Patek and Audemars Piguet.

stops.name: Kamakura
stops.note: Coastal temple town with Daibutsu, Hase-dera, and the Enoden line

stops.name: Engaku-ji
stops.note: Rinzai Zen temple climbing a wooded hillside right at Kita-Kamakura station, with a Muso Soseki garden and a famous bell; ¥500, 8:00–16:30.

stops.name: Meigetsu-in
stops.note: Rinzai Zen temple in Kita-Kamakura with a dry rock garden in front of the main hall and the famous round "window of enlightenment" looking onto the inner garden; ¥500, 9:00–16:00.

stops.name: Kencho-ji
stops.note: Japan's oldest Zen training monastery (1253) and first of Kamakura's Five Great Zen Temples: vast gate, bell, and a pond garden by Muso Soseki behind the abbot's hall; ¥500, 8:30–16:30.

stops.name: Hokoku-ji
stops.note: Small Rinzai Zen temple known for its bamboo grove, a dry rock garden and a teahouse where you drink matcha inside the bamboo; ¥400 plus tea, 9:00–16:00.

stops.name: Jomyo-ji
stops.note: Fifth of the Kamakura Five Great Zen Temples, with a raked dry-landscape garden viewed from the Kisen-an teahouse over a bowl of matcha; ¥100 plus tea, 9:00–16:30.

stops.name: Zuisen-ji
stops.note: Muso Soseki's 1327 rock garden cut into the cliff behind the hall, plus a flower garden; ¥200, 9:00–17:00.

stops.name: Kotoku-in (Great Buddha)
stops.note: The 13-metre bronze Great Buddha of 1252, sitting in the open since its hall was washed away in 1498; ¥300, 8:00–17:00 in October, ¥50 more to step inside it.

stops.name: Hase-dera
stops.note: Hillside temple of the eleven-headed Kannon with a pond garden below and a terrace looking over Yuigahama beach and the bay; ¥400, 8:00–16:30 in October.

stops.name: Nezu Shrine
stops.note: Quiet shrine with a red torii tunnel

stops.name: Yanaka Ginza
stops.note: Traditional shopping street famous for its resident cats, cat-themed shops, and old-Tokyo atmosphere.

stops.name: Hinoya
stops.note: Multi-brand denim strip

stops.name: Pigment Tokyo
stops.note: Gallery-store of ~4,500 pigments

stops.name: teamLab Planets
stops.note: Barefoot immersive digital-art museum

stops.name: Alvark Tokyo vs Ibaraki — Thu 22 Oct
stops.note: B.League Premier home game at Toyota Arena Tokyo, tip-off 19:05. Second night of Alvark Entertainment Special 3DAYS.

stops.name: Mizutani Camera
stops.note: Secondhand camera and watch dealer under a blue awning across from Ueno station's south exit, trading vintage Seiko and Citizen alongside Rolex and Omega. Reported to be English-speaking and tax-free registered.

stops.name: Quark Ueno
stops.note: Quark's main Rolex store in Ueno, stocking new, used and vintage references with buying and selling under one roof.

stops.name: Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo
stops.note: Tokyo's main contemporary collection, at 4-1-1 Miyoshi in Kiba Park: about 5,600 works charting art from 1945 on, plus six to eight changing shows a year spanning architecture, fashion and design. Open 10:00-18:00, last entry 17:30, closed Mondays; around ¥1,300. Ten minutes on foot from Kiyosumi-Shirakawa station.

stops.name: Yayoi Kusama Museum
stops.note: Small dedicated museum for Kusama's polka-dot infinity installations

stops.name: Meiji Jingu
stops.note: Forest shrine inside the city

stops.name: Otter cafe (Harry)
stops.note: Otters, hedgehogs, chinchillas

stops.name: Fullcount Tokyo
stops.note: Osaka Five heritage raw-denim brand

stops.name: Studio D'Artisan
stops.note: Original "Osaka Five" label

stops.name: Samurai Jeans
stops.note: Heavyweight raw denim, est. 1997

stops.name: Pure Blue Japan Harajuku
stops.note: Cult Japanese denim brand specializing in slubby, textured selvedge with dramatic fading potential.

stops.name: Five G Music Technology
stops.note: Legendary vintage synth + eurorack shop

stops.name: Momotaro Jeans Aoyama
stops.note: Flagship store for Momotaro's premium Japanese selvedge denim, known for the peach logo and Zimbabwe cotton.

stops.name: Nezu Museum Garden
stops.note: Kengo Kuma's museum of East Asian art with a steep, mossy garden of stone lanterns, teahouses and a pond; museum ticket required, closed Mondays, 10:00–17:00.

stops.name: Hachiko Commemorative Stamp
stops.note: Eki-stamp at SHIBU HACHI BOX tourist info center near Hachiko statue

stops.name: Miyashita Park
stops.note: Rooftop park over the shopping deck

stops.name: Echigoya Music
stops.note: Vintage synths + eurorack, near Tower Records

stops.name: Shibuya Sky
stops.note: Open-air rooftop observation deck

stops.name: ZAKURO SHOW — October 23, 2026
stops.note: October 23, 2026 bilingual one-hour live concert featuring taiko alongside koto, shamisen, shakuhachi and other traditional Japanese instruments.

stops.name: The Real McCoy's Tokyo
stops.note: Tokyo flagship at 6-25-8 Jingumae, on the Meiji-dori side of Cat Street between Harajuku and Shibuya; open daily 12:00-20:00. Reproduction A-2 and N-1 flight jackets, Buco motorcycle gear, Joe McCoy workwear and Lot 001 denim, all made in Japan.

stops.name: United Arrows Harajuku Main Store
stops.note: The original main store in Jingumae, ground floor and basement, the shop the company grew out of after leaving Beams in 1989. Sources disagree on the current address (3-28-1 and 2-31-12 Jingumae both appear) and one listing reports a renovation closure.

stops.name: Taro Okamoto Memorial Museum
stops.note: The artist's own house and studio at 6-1-19 Minami-Aoyama, left as it was: the working studio with brushes and half-finished canvases, and a small garden crowded with his sculptures. Open 10:00-18:00, last entry 17:30, closed Tuesdays; ¥650 adults, ¥300 for children.

stops.name: Kapital Ebisu
stops.note: Multi-floor flagship for Kapital's patchwork denim, boro-inspired pieces, and Americana-meets-Japan aesthetic. The 2-20-2 Ebisu-minami address (Gaia Ebisu Building) now also appears as the KAPITAL Tokyo Naked Store, 11:00–20:00.

stops.name: Kapital Legs Ebisu
stops.note: The bottoms-only Kapital shop a few minutes from the flagship, in the Ebisu Sunny Building at 2-23-12 Ebisu-minami; said to stock more than a hundred jeans styles.

stops.name: Kapital Duffle
stops.note: Denim-led lifestyle store at 2-24-2 Ebisu-minami with homewares and original goods, plus exhibitions, workshops and pop-ups.

stops.name: Iron Heart
stops.note: Heavyweight workwear denim

stops.name: Kapital Ginza
stops.note: Kapital's Ginza store on the 1st and 3rd floors of the Shimaharu Building, 1-21-12 Ginza, at the Kyobashi end of the district.

stops.name: Lemon-sha Ginza
stops.note: 40-year Ginza camera institution with film cameras, fountain pens, and watches

stops.name: Itoya Ginza
stops.note: Twelve floors of stationery at 2-7-15 Ginza since 1904: paper by the sheet, fountain pens, inks, notebooks, letterpress and a floor you can have cards printed on; 10:00-20:00.

stops.name: Ginza Tsuboyaki-imo
stops.note: Pot-roasted sweet potato specialist using traditional clay-jar method

stops.name: Imperial Palace East Gardens
stops.note: The old Edo Castle inner grounds: massive stone walls, the keep base and the Ninomaru stroll garden; free, closed Mondays and Fridays, gates close 16:30 in October.

stops.name: Azabudai Hills Sky Lobby
stops.note: Free 34th-floor Sky Lobby in Tokyo's newest skyscraper (2023), with floor-to-ceiling windows and Tokyo Tower views.

stops.name: Zojo-ji
stops.note: Head temple of Jodo Buddhism in Tokyo, its main hall framed by Tokyo Tower, with the Tokugawa shogun graves behind; grounds free, about 9:00–17:00.

stops.name: Kapital SOHO Roppongi
stops.note: Kapital's Roppongi Hills shop, Hill Side 1F at 6-10-1 Roppongi, open 11:00–20:00.

stops.name: Kapital Legs Roppongi
stops.note: Second Kapital shop inside Roppongi Hills Hill Side, bottoms-focused like its Ebisu namesake.

stops.name: United Arrows Roppongi Hills
stops.note: United Arrows' largest store, West Walk 2-3F at 6-10-3 Roppongi: womenswear on the lower floor, the full men's range on the upper. Open 11:00-20:00, until 21:00 on Fridays and Saturdays.

stops.name: The National Art Center, Tokyo
stops.note: Kisho Kurokawa's 2007 building at 7-22-2 Roppongi, a rippling glass wall with inverted concrete cones inside and no permanent collection, only touring shows. Open 10:00-18:00 and until 20:00 on Fridays and Saturdays for its own exhibitions, closed Tuesdays. The building itself is free to walk into.

stops.name: Edo Taito Traditional Crafts Center
stops.note: Free traditional-crafts center displaying hundreds of examples of Tokyo handicrafts, with regular artisan demonstrations and occasional hands-on programs.

stops.name: cafe capyba ASAKUSA
stops.note: Dedicated capybara cafe where you can sit with, pet, photograph, and feed capybaras.
